slides.0.title: Appellations and the Quality Pyramid
slides.0.subtitle: From Côtes du Rhône to the stand-alone crus
slides.1.title: The quality pyramid
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Base: Côtes du Rhône
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Covers 172 communes across six départements (WineWithSeth, 2025), about 26,800 ha in 2025; the most flexible and largest tier
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Côtes du Rhône Villages
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Limited to 95 communes in four southern départements, with stricter rules; about 8,000 ha in 2025
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Villages + a place name
slides.1.highlights.2.content: 21 villages may add their name to the label (e.g. Plan de Dieu, Séguret), still within the Côtes du Rhône Villages AOC
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Top: the crus
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Each cru is its own stand-alone AOC; there are now 18 (Laudun became the 18th in 2024)
slides.1.content: Moving up the pyramid, areas shrink, rules tighten and style becomes more local — the structure the Diploma tests most.
slides.2.title: The 8 northern crus
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Côte-Rôtie
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Red; Syrah-based, with a little Viognier allowed
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Condrieu and Château-Grillet
slides.2.highlights.1.content: White; 100% Viognier. Château-Grillet is a single-estate AOC of only about 4 ha (Inter Rhône 2024)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Hermitage and Crozes-Hermitage
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Red and white; Hermitage is a famed hill of about 136 ha, Crozes-Hermitage the largest northern cru (about 2,100 ha)
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Saint-Joseph, Cornas and Saint-Péray
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Saint-Joseph (red and white, about 1,400 ha); Cornas (red, 100% Syrah); Saint-Péray (white, including sparkling)
slides.2.content: Areas are from Inter Rhône Key Figures (2024 data), for scale only.
slides.3.title: The 10 southern crus
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The southern Rhône's emblematic cru, red and white, AOC 1936, with many permitted grapes
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Gigondas and Vacqueyras
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Red-wine appellations beneath the Dentelles de Montmirail, Grenache-led
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Vinsobres, Cairanne, Rasteau, Beaumes-de-Venise
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Promoted to cru in turn: Beaumes-de-Venise 2005, Vinsobres 2006, Rasteau 2010, Cairanne 2016
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Lirac, Tavel and Laudun
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Tavel is the cru devoted solely to rosé; Lirac makes red, white and rosé; Laudun became the 18th cru in 2024
slides.3.content: Dates cross-check WineWithSeth and Decanter; older dates (e.g. 1971, 1990) will be checked against INAO in Level 2 before being tested.
slides.4.title: Sweet VDN and outlying names
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Two VDN
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Inter Rhône lists two vins doux naturels: Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise and Rasteau VDN
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Names that are not crus
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Ventoux, Luberon, Grignan-les-Adhémar, Côtes du Vivarais, Clairette de Die and others are further AOCs within the Rhône family, not among the 18 crus
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Costières de Nîmes
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Geographically in the Gard next to Languedoc, but INAO has placed it under the Rhône committee since 2004 and Inter Rhône counts it; the course treats it only briefly, outside the northern/southern crus
slides.4.content: "The Rhône family" can be drawn administratively or geographically; state which basis you use for border cases.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Which tier sits at the top of the pyramid?
Each cru is its own AOC with the strictest rules, at the top.
How many crus does the Rhône now have (8 north + 10 south)?
Inter Rhône shows 18 Côtes du Rhône crus, with Laudun the 18th in 2024.
Which of these is a northern Rhône cru?
Cornas is in the north; the other three are southern.
Tavel is the Rhône's only cru devoted to rosé.
